definitions.explanation: An arrangement to record purchases and settle the total later rather than paying each time; by extension, the negative consequences of past actions that eventually come due.

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}にツケがたまっている。
examples.english: I have an unpaid tab at the shop.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いころの{無理|むり}のツケが{今|いま}になって{回|まわ}ってきた。
examples.english: The price of overdoing it when I was young has finally caught up with me.

notes:
Usually written in katakana as ツケ (also {付|つ}け). Refers to buying now and paying later on a running account, a practice once common at neighborhood bars and shops.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ツケで{買|か}う: to buy on credit / on a tab
- ツケがたまる: for an unpaid tab to build up
- ツケを{払|はら}う: to settle the tab
- ツケが{回|まわ}ってくる: for past excesses to catch up with one

USAGE:
The figurative sense — the {代償|だいしょう} (price) of earlier carelessness coming due — is very common, especially in ツケが{回|まわ}ってくる.
